question: Find the difference between the simple interest and the compound interest payable annually on a sum of Rs. 6,500 at 7% per annum for 3 years. (Correct to two decimal places.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 3 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by: D = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100)

Substituting the values: D = 6500 × (7/100)² × (3 + 7/100)

D = 6500 × (49/10000) × (3.07)

D = 31.85 × 3.07 = 97.7795

Rounding to two decimal places, we get ₹97.78.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹97.78.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Difference (CI − SI) for 3 Years

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹6,500

Rate (R) = 7% per annum

Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Difference (D) = P × (R/100)² × [(300 + R)/100]

**Calculations:**

⇒ D = 6500 × (7/100)² × [(300 + 7)/100]

⇒ D = 6500 × (49/10000) × (307/100)

⇒ D = (6500 × 49 × 307) ÷ 1000000

⇒ D = (65 × 49 × 307) ÷ 10000

⇒ D = (3185 × 307) ÷ 10000

⇒ D = 977795 ÷ 10000

⇒ D = ₹97.7795

⇒ D ≈ ₹97.78

**∴ The correct answer is ₹97.78.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference for 2 years

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is D = P(R/100)².

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For 3 years, the effective CI rate is 3R + 3R²/100 + R³/10000. For R=7%, Effective Rate = 22.5043%.

Relationship between CI and SI

For the first year (if compounded annually), CI = SI. From the second year onwards, CI > SI because interest is earned on interest.
